input.quote: Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use
input.rationale: The grant already extends to Sparkling's affiliated companies (at Authorized Locations) without any notice condition, and the licence is not revocable at Garman's discretion (Section 17(a) makes it perpetual while fees are paid, with termination only on insolvency or uncured material default, converting to a fee-free perpetual licence on Garman's default). However, the licence is expressly \"non-transferable\" and Section 3(c) bars any transfer without Garman's written consent, so the fallback element of transferability to a successor in a merger or acquisition fails on a material term. We therefore target the fallback: the licence remains non-exclusive but is transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction, with a matching carve-out in the Section 3(c) restriction so no contradictory prohibition is retained. The broader assignment consent in Section 20(d) is left untouched as an ASSIGN matter.

mappings.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
mappings.quote: for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations

mappings.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.

proposal.summary: Make the licence transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position requires the licence to survive a corporate transaction, so we made it transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition and carved that transfer out of the Section 3(c) transfer restriction; affiliate coverage already in the grant is acceptable.
